doc.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Getting John Levy as manager
summary: She explains the logistics burden, how Levy took her on for helping people, and that they have no contract.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: the logistics of the phone calls, the money, the contracts, being on top of it, and now I’ve finally just got a manager so that’s going to be much better.
I heard that. You got John Levy to be your manager.
Yeah. Who’d you hear that from?
Well I heard it from Bob I think.
And I know John, because Joe Williams actually helped us start this interview process.
And so John visited the college and I actually got to interview John and he is, I’m pleased to hear that you’ve got an association with him.

I’m so excited, I’m just like so happy. I mean I called them for a recommendation. I never in a million years thought he’d take me on. And I sat down with him and I said — you know because then they wanted to meet, he and Devra Hall, his wife, and so we were talking and I said, I showed him my whole schedule for the year. I said, “well I know this is peanuts.” You know, he’s worked with all the greats. What I make, financially, and can bring to them is nothing. So I said, “I realize this isn’t much.” And he said, “no, no, no,” he said, “I only look at two things, if I can help somebody and if I like them.” And I could tell he really meant that. And that was just so nice to hear. Because I don’t know how many — I think most managers are looking at how much money is she making, is it enough to really make it worth my while. Of course practically you have to do that. But I’m sure a lot of his success through the years has been that — that must feel so great for the artists that work with him to feel that that’s what’s behind his motivation.
Right. Joe spoke very, very highly of him. They had a relationship for so many years and they said it was just on a handshake and that they just —

Actually we haven’t even signed a contract yet. They started working with me and there’s no contact now. I’m sure there will be. I don’t care. I never had a contract with my record company really. After a while for my records, but we had this other record out for months and we haven’t even done the publishing contract yet. It’s just — but I like to work with people that I trust and they trust me.
